name: Easter
seo_title: Easter Charcuterie Board Ideas (Nest, Egg + Brunch)
description: Easter charcuterie board ideas: an Easter brunch board with ham, a bird's-nest board, an egg-shaped board, a pastel board for kids, and how much to buy.
answer: An Easter board is usually brunch or a pre-dinner snack, so plan about 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest, use spring colors (strawberries, snap peas, radishes, pastel candy), and add the foods of the day: deviled eggs, sliced ham and hot cross buns. A nest or egg shape makes it the photo of the day.

ideas.title: The Easter Brunch Board
ideas.text: Sliced glazed ham and prosciutto, deviled eggs, Brie and Havarti, hot cross buns or brioche, strawberries, melon and a pot of honey.

ideas.title: The Bird's Nest Board
ideas.text: A ring of pretzels and crackers as the nest, filled with mozzarella balls and speckled chocolate eggs, surrounded by salami, cheese and spring vegetables.

ideas.title: The Pastel Kids' Board
ideas.text: Mild cheese cut with a bunny cookie cutter, ham roll-ups, strawberries, grapes, pastel candy and graham crackers.

shapes.name: Easter Egg Board
steps: On a large oval or round board, outline an egg shape with crackers.
Fill it in stripes: strawberries, cheddar, snap peas, white cheese, purple grapes.
Tuck mint or edible flowers between the stripes.

shapes.name: Bird's Nest Board
steps: Make a ring of pretzel sticks and crackers in the center of a round board.
Fill the nest with mozzarella balls, mini cheese rounds or chocolate eggs.
Build the rest of the board around it with ham, salami, cheese and spring vegetables.

plan.what: Buy crackers, candy, nuts and jarred items.
Hard-boil the eggs and make the deviled egg filling. Keep both in the fridge.
Slice ham and cheese, wash fruit, fill and chill the deviled eggs.
Take hard cheese out of the fridge, then build the board. Add the deviled eggs last on a chilled plate.

faq.q: What goes on an Easter charcuterie board?
faq.a: Sliced ham and prosciutto, deviled eggs, mild spring cheeses like Brie and Havarti, hot cross buns or brioche, strawberries and melon, spring vegetables, and a little pastel candy or chocolate eggs.

faq.q: How do you make a bird's nest charcuterie board?
faq.a: Make a ring of pretzel sticks and crackers in the middle of a round board, fill it with mozzarella balls or chocolate eggs, and build the rest of the board around it.

faq.q: Can deviled eggs go on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: Yes. Set them on a chilled plate or a tray over ice at one end, and keep them out no more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F). Make the filling the day before and fill the eggs the morning of.

faq.q: How much ham do I need for an Easter board?
faq.a: On a mixed board, about 1 oz of ham per guest as one of two or three meats, inside the 2 oz-per-guest meat total. If ham is also the main course, keep the board light.

faq.q: What cheese is good for an Easter board?
faq.a: Mild, fresh-tasting cheeses suit spring: Brie, Havarti, fresh goat cheese and a young cheddar. Add one aged cheese for contrast.

faq.q: How much does an Easter charcuterie board cost?
faq.a: Before a meal, plan about $3 to $5 per guest on a budget and $5 to $8 for a standard board, so roughly $35 to $60 or $60 to $95 for 12 guests. Splurge cheeses and meats run $12 or more per guest. Store and region change the total.

faq.q: How far ahead can I make an Easter charcuterie board?
faq.a: Shop for crackers, nuts and jars a week ahead and for cheese, meat and fruit 2 days ahead. The morning of, slice the cheese and fold the meats, then cover and chill. Build the board in the last hour, with the deviled eggs on a chilled plate added last, adding crackers last so they stay crisp.

ahead: 1 week: crackers, candy, nuts and jarred items
1 day: hard-boil the eggs and make the deviled egg filling
The morning of: slice ham and cheese, wash fruit, fill the deviled eggs and chill
last: Put deviled eggs out last, on a chilled plate
Take hard cheese out an hour before; soft cheese 20 to 30 minutes
